questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past?
options: I have lost my keys yesterday.
I have lost my keys.
I lost my keys.
I had lost my keys.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form of the adjective 'busy'.
options: busier
more busy
busiest
busierest

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct first conditional structure.
options: If it rains, I will stay at home.
If it rained, I would stay at home.
If it rains, I will have stayed at home.
If it has rained, I will stay at home.
questions.answer: If it rains, I will stay at home.

questions.question: Which option uses the gerund correctly as the subject of the sentence?
options: Swimming is good for your heart.
To swim is good for your heart.
Swam is good for your heart.
Swim is good for your heart.
questions.answer: Swimming is good for your heart.

questions.question: Select the sentence that correctly uses a modal verb to give advice.
options: You must drink more water.
You should drink more water.
You can drink more water.
You would drink more water.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the past continuous to describe an action that was interrupted?
options: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
I slept when the phone rang.
I had been sleeping when the phone rang.
I was sleep when the phone rang.
questions.answer: I was sleeping when the phone rang.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that uses the correct linker to show contrast.
options: It was raining, but we went for a walk.
It was raining, so we went for a walk.
It was raining, therefore we went for a walk.
It was raining, because we went for a walk.
questions.answer: It was raining, but we went for a walk.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct infinitive form.
options: She decided to go to the cinema.
She decided going to the cinema.
She decided go to the cinema.
She decided of going to the cinema.
questions.answer: She decided to go to the cinema.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the superlative form of the adjective 'expensive'?
options: This is the most expensive car.
This is more expensive car.
This is the expensive car.
This is the most expensively car.
questions.answer: This is the most expensive car.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the third conditional to talk about a past possibility that did not happen.
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would pass the exam.
If I studied harder, I will pass the exam.
questions.answer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
